calls.head: Quality over quantity for the Penguins
calls.body: The Penguins make their shots count, and the Canadiens are one of the league’s worst at preventing dangerous shots. Expect the Penguins to get some real chances.
calls.call: The Penguins’ average shot has at least their usual 6.7% chance of going in.
calls.nums: Pittsburgh 5th for shot quality (a 6.7% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Montréal 30th for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: Pittsburgh’s average shot had a 5.8% chance of going in, against their usual 6.7%.

calls.head: Special teams lean toward the Penguins
calls.body: The Canadiens’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Penguins’ power play is near the top of the league. Discipline matters more than usual for the Canadiens tonight.
calls.call: The Penguins’ power play creates at least their usual 7.6 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: Pittsburgh 10th for power play (7.6 expected goals per 60) · Montréal 27th for penalty kill
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: Pittsburgh’s power play created 9.4 expected goals per 60 in 5:07 of 5-on-4 time, against their usual 7.6, and scored 2 goals.

PIT.head: We had this close to even (57% for Pittsburgh), and Pittsburgh came through.

MTL.head: We had this close to even (43% for Montréal), and it went Pittsburgh’s way.

surprises.head: A rough night for J. Dobes
surprises.body: J. Dobes allowed 6 goals on shots worth 2.8 expected goals, 3.2 more than expected. Starting goalies had a night this rough about once every 40 starts over the last three seasons.

surprises.head: Pittsburgh shortened their bench
surprises.body: Pittsburgh’s bottom-six forwards played 40% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 44% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 10 games.

story.head: Novak wins it in overtime
paras: Cole Caufield opened the scoring early in the first. Tommy Novak added two goals. Five different Penguins scored. The game was tied twice. Novak won it 1:33 into overtime.
The Canadiens had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Canadiens win about six in ten. By our Swing measure, Nick Suzuki had the best night of anyone, even in a loss.

items.text: One of the preview’s two calls held.
